question.problem:
Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the following probability density function:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}x, & 0<x<4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

If the probability density function of $Y=\frac{1}{2}|X-1|$ is given by 

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}g(y), & 0<y<\frac{1}{2} \\ h(y), & \frac{1}{2}\le y<\frac{3}{2} \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

find the function $g(y).$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's visualize the transformation $Y=\frac{1}{2}|X-1|$ over the interval $0<x<4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14231916/assets/163ffe5a4c5bcbce95369f8082c8dbfababe7c40315d8136d79c9e370f05a1a1.png)

Notice the following:

- The transformation is two-to-one over the interval $0<x<2.$ On this interval, $Y$ is nonzero on $0<y<\frac{1}{2}.$

- The transformation is one-to-one over the interval $2\le x<4.$ On this interval,  $Y$ is nonzero on  $\frac{1}{2}\le y<\frac{3}{2}.$

In this question, we're asked to consider only the interval $0<y<\frac{1}{2}.$ 

Using the definition of the cumulative distribution of $Y,$ for $0<y<\frac{1}{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{Y}(y) & =P(Y\le y) \\  & =P(\frac{1}{2}|X-1|\le y) \\  & =P(|X-1|\le 2y) \\  & =P(-2y\le X-1\le 2y) \\  & =P(1-2y\le X\le 2y+1) \\  & ={F}_{X}(2y+1)-{F}_{X}(1-2y).\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the PDF ${f}_{Y}(y)$ for $0<y<\frac{1}{2},$ we differentiate ${F}_{Y}$ with respect to $y$ using the chain rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={F}_{Y}^{′}(y) \\  & =2{F}_{X}^{′}(2y+1)+2{F}_{X}^{′}(1-2y) \\  & =2{f}_{X}(2y+1)+2{f}_{X}(1-2y) \\  & =2({f}_{X}(2y+1)+{f}_{X}(1-2y)).\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the definition of ${f}_{X},$ we finally arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & =2({f}_{X}(2y+1)+{f}_{X}(1-2y)) \\  & =2(\frac{1}{8}(2y+1)+\frac{1}{8}(1-2y)) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $g(y)=\frac{1}{2}.$
